turns.assistant:
**Answer**

A queue is a waiting line for tasks. New work goes in at the back. The system takes work from the front and runs it one piece at a time.

**Why**

This order is first-in, first-out (FIFO). The oldest waiting task gets handled next. That keeps work fair and predictable.

A queue also smooths bursts. Producers can add work faster than workers finish it. The queue holds the extra until a worker is free.

Workers pull from the front when ready. If nothing is waiting, the worker sits idle. If work piles up, the line grows until workers catch up.

**Example**

Three print jobs arrive: A, then B, then C. The printer finishes A first, then B, then C. C never jumps ahead of A or B.
